title: Largest Account Total
statement:
A small bank keeps a table balances. Row i belongs to customer i, and column j is how much that customer holds in bank branch j.

A customer's total is the sum of their row. Return the largest total of any customer.

examples.why: Totals are 7, 6 and 6. The 6 in the last row is the biggest single cell, but not the biggest total.
Totals 11, 12 and 10. The customer holding the 9 is not the richest.

gen: (r, big) => [r.matrix(big ? 50 : r.int(1, 5), big ? 50 : r.int(1, 5), big ? 1 : 0, big ? 100 : 9)]
hints: Sum each row, and keep the largest sum you have seen.

explain.intuition:
Each customer's total depends only on their own row, so the problem splits into "sum a row" and "keep a running maximum". There is no shortcut: every cell can change the answer, so every cell must be read once.

It is the same shape as finding the busiest day in a table of hourly counts: reduce each row, then reduce the results.
steps: For each row, add up its values.
If that sum is bigger than best, update best.
pitfalls: Taking the biggest single cell instead of the biggest row sum.

solutions.title: Row sums with a running maximum
solutions.idea: Sum every row and keep the largest.

followups: Return the index of the richest customer, picking the smallest index on ties.
The table arrives as a stream of (customer, branch, amount) entries in random order. How do you find the richest customer?
